newsitem.title: USA: NAFTA dairy panel leak harms dispute process--USTR.
newsitem.headline: NAFTA dairy panel leak harms dispute process--USTR.

text.p: U.S. trade ambassador Ira Shapiro said Wednesday leaks of a preliminary ruling on U.S.-Canada trade in dairy, eggs and poultry products had compromised a NAFTA dispute resolution process.
The initial panel report was delivered to the two governments July 15, and the finding was widely reported to have been in Canada's favor. U.S. officials have said Canada leaked the initial report.
"We regret that all parties have not respected the confidentiality rules," Shapiro told a House agriculture subcommittee hearing.
"To the extent they (the rules) are ignored, the overall integrity of the system is damaged," U.S. Trade Representative negotiator Shapiro said.

The final report by the North American Free Trade Agreement panel, which was due out in August, will be released in late November, in part to allow the two sides to submit further arguments to the five-member panel, Shapiro said.
Gus Schumacher, the administrator of the U.S. Agriculture Department's Foreign Agriculture Service, said the delay could be viewed as hopeful for the United States.
"The fact that they've delayed until November their final submission means that ... hopefully they will be reconsidering their legal views on this," Schumacher told reporters.

Under the World Trade Organization rules, Canada converted quotas for dairy, eggs and poultry product imports to tariffs. The United States argued that these tariffs should be zero for U.S. products under NAFTA.
